newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian linear bonds to remain in doldrums.
newsitem.headline: Belgian linear bonds to remain in doldrums.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds were likely to remain becalmed for the foreseeable future after passing a very quiet day on Thursday, traders said.
"It has been a non-day. The end of the year (lull) has already started," one said.
Traders said there had been some activity in the 2003 OLO, with a spate of selling followed by a rush of buying, but end-investors had kept their hands in their pockets throughout the day.
Holders of paper do not want to sell for tax reasons, while others are strapped for cash and cannot buy.
Traders said there had been a flattening of the yield curve in the 10-20 year maturities as well as in the five and six year maturities in common with German Bunds.
They said U.S. jobless figures had initially sparked some selling but the market soon bounced back as buying had emerged.

Likewise the allegations facing Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo that he had sex with under-age boys, and the evident strain that is creating within the country's centre-left coalition government, had been discounted by the market as unlikely to cause the coalition's breakup.
"The government will fight to keep itself together," one trader said.
The benchmark 2006 OLO ended unchanged from Wednesday, yielding 5.99 percent. The spread over Bunds was likewise static at 16 basis points.
The December futures contract was just three basis points easier at 120.17.
